objections.author: openai
objections.target: TV-05 and TV-07 — no-transformation / lost-evidence impossibility claims
objections.claim: These sentences assert a general observed-data impossibility, and TV-05 says the paper 'show[s]' it. That is not earned by the paper's derivation or simulations and directly conflicts with G4, which states that no argument here shows that no estimator built from the same observed data could do better. The supported claim is only that the studied corrected criteria/tests exhibit residual information loss as measured through these corrections.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Replace with scoped wording such as: 'For the corrected criterion and calibrated-test procedures studied here, the better-fit case retains a residual shortfall attributable to missing information; this analysis does not rule out a different observed-data estimator recovering more.'

objections.author: openai
objections.target: TV-10 — recommendation to add the per-candidate trace correction for nested comparisons
objections.claim: The recommendation conflates IC ranking with LRT/nested comparison. The paper's own LRT result says the nested-comparison bias is tr(RIV_perp) in the tested directions and that the difference of per-candidate corrections always overstates it; a calibrated reference distribution already carries the null mean. The clause 'no calibrated reference distribution already absorbs the bias' does not justify using the per-candidate difference for nested comparisons.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Split the rule: for information-criterion ranking, add each candidate's trace correction; for calibrated LRTs, leave the numerator uncorrected; for any uncalibrated nested-comparison correction, use the tested-direction object tr(RIV_perp), not the difference of per-candidate traces.

objections.author: openai
objections.target: TV-01, TV-02, TV-09, TV-11, and TV-12 — abstract/conclusion decision-level summaries
objections.claim: The prose upgrades an expectation-level trace correction and scoped simulation recoveries into broad decision-level language: 'complete-data-equivalent selection,' 'behave as they would have with complete data,' 'trust the result,' and deterministic favoring of 'more complex' or highest-missing-information candidates. The paper establishes correction of the expected criterion under stated conditions, substantial but incomplete selection recovery, and null/equal-fit calibration; realized rankings still depend on fit, penalties, signal strength, and candidate geometry, and complexity is not generally proved to imply larger RIV.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Use calibrated wording: 'corrects the expected criterion under the stated MI/estimated-scale conditions,' 'substantially improves or restores rankings in the studied congenial nested designs,' 'all else equal favors larger-RIV candidates,' and 'trust subject to the stated congeniality, model-family, and weak-signal limitations.'

objections.author: openai
objections.target: TV-03, TV-04, and TV-08 — universal bias/removal language
objections.claim: The wording 'every deviance and every information criterion,' 'removes the bias,' and 'the bias exists only when the fit estimates a scale or covariance' is broader than the established object. The derivation concerns the averaged Q/log-likelihood and likelihood-based criteria under congenial proper MI with an estimated scale/covariance; the trace term is accompanied by the design-imbalance term (A)+(C), and the same paragraph notes a distinct -1/2 tr(RIV) bias for known-scale proper MI. The defense relies on a narrowed meaning of 'the bias' that is not explicit in the sentences.
objections.what_would_satisfy: State the object explicitly: 'For the averaged deviance/Q-based IC in the estimated-scale case, the positive optimism term is proportional to tr(RIV), with the separate (A)+(C) term vanishing under MCAR; the trace correction removes that trace component, and the full bias only under the stated conditions. Known-scale proper MI has a distinct negative term.'

objections.author: openai
objections.target: TV-13 — 'bounds the cost of not running data augmentation'
objections.claim: The engine-sensitivity study is an empirical agreement check on selected demanding designs. Agreement within 2–3% on tr(RIV) and 0.011 on the recovery gap does not constitute a formal bound on the unrun data-augmentation alternative. 'Bounds' implies a guaranteed inequality or worst-case control that the paper does not establish.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Replace 'bounds' with 'empirically estimates,' 'suggests,' or 'in these studied designs, found little additional cost'; retain the caveat that fully Bayesian data augmentation remains the conservative choice when missing information is large.

objections.author: openai
objections.target: TV-14 and TV-15 — congenial-cell qualifier and 'all sixty cells'
objections.claim: The intro/result prose drops or blurs the key qualifier. The supported statement is that in every congenial cell, all uncorrected MI-AIC errors land on the saturated, largest-missing-information candidate. Saying 'every misclassification' without 'congenial' and then 'held across all sixty cells' can be read as applying the same all-errors pattern to uncongenial cells, despite the disclosed uncongenial overshoot.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Write: 'In every congenial cell, all uncorrected MI-AIC errors chose the saturated, largest-RIV candidate.' If a broader directional prediction held across all 60 cells, state that separately and distinguish it from the stronger congenial-cell all-errors pattern.

objections.author: openai
objections.target: TV-16 and TV-17 — workflow counterfactual and historical-cause claim
objections.claim: The observed fact that 8 of 9 blind cross-family re-derivations initially produced the opposite sign supports the value of the cross-family check, but it does not establish the counterfactual that a single-family workflow would likely have shipped the wrong sign. Likewise, documenting that prior MI model-selection questions were open/thin does not establish the singular cause that they were open because the second and third levels had not been posed.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Recast as evidence and interpretation rather than established fact: 'In our blind cross-family check, 8 of 9 derivations initially took the opposite sign, illustrating a sign fork that a less diverse check might miss' and 'posing the second and third levels reframes these open questions,' unless additional historical/process evidence is supplied.

objections.author: openai
objections.target: TV-18, TV-19, and TV-20 — literature scope and reader-followable citations
objections.claim: The literature/future-work prose is not sufficiently reader-verifiable as written. 'Only one information criterion has been proposed for multiply imputed data' needs its scope narrowed to the averaged-imputed-data IC class, otherwise it reads in tension with the later Claeskens-Consentino and Hens routes. The named Satorra-Bentler arm needs a local citation or clear cross-reference if S4 is the support. 'Developed separately' points to companion or external work but provides no citation or cross-reference.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Amend to 'Only one averaged-criterion IC for multiply imputed data of the kind considered here...' with the Consentino-Claeskens citation and a cross-reference distinguishing adjacent routes; add a Satorra-Bentler/Asparouhov-Muthen/Satorra citation or cross-reference at S5; cite the companion/sequel for the separately developed methods or change the sentence to 'are left for future work.'

objections.author: gemini
objections.claim: The sentences assert an absolute impossibility ('no transformation of the observed data can recover it' / 'No transformation of the observed data manufactures the lost evidence back') which directly contradicts the G4 limitation ('No argument here shows that no estimator built from the same observed data could do better'). Defending the text AS-IS while conceding the paper's explicit limitation is a buried contradiction.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Amend TV-05 and TV-07 to explicitly restrict the claim to Information Criteria / likelihood methods (e.g., 'as measured through these corrections'), removing the absolute 'no transformation of the observed data' language.

objections.author: gemini
objections.claim: The instruction to 'add the per-candidate trace correction' when the aim is to 'compare nested models' directly contradicts the paper's own LRT result (S1-P6b), which establishes that the difference of per-candidate corrections ALWAYS OVERSTATES the nested-comparison bias (tr(RIV_perp)). Advising the per-candidate trace for nested models conflates IC ranking with nested testing.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Remove 'or to compare nested models' from the instruction advocating the per-candidate trace correction, making it clear that nested comparisons require the perpendicular reference distribution correction.

objections.author: gemini
objections.claim: The word 'bounds' implies a formalized or derived mathematical limit, but the advocate admits the check is merely an empirical agreement measurement on selected cells. An empirical observation does not 'bound' the theoretical cost.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Replace 'bounds' with an empirically appropriate term such as 'empirically estimates', 'assesses', or 'measures'.

objections.author: gemini
objections.claim: TV-20 points to methods 'developed separately' without providing any citation or cross-reference. TV-19 names an external test ('Satorra-Bentler arm') without a citation upon introduction. This explicitly fails the citation_support bar.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Add a pre-print, working paper, or explicit cross-reference citation for the work 'developed separately', and add the appropriate literature citation at the sentence for Satorra-Bentler in S5.

objections.author: gemini
objections.claim: TV-14 asserts unqualifiedly in the abstract/intro that 'every misclassification... chose the candidate with the largest RIV', and TV-15 claims the directional prediction held across 'all sixty cells'. Both omit the critical 'congenial cell' limitation established in the results section, contradicting the known uncongenial overshoot.
objections.what_would_satisfy: Add the modifier 'In congenial simulations' to TV-14, and accurately scope TV-15 to distinguish between the congenial subset and the full sixty cells.

OBJ-03.sustained_point: The amendment still overgeneralizes TV-02: "in nested families, the more complex models" states a general complexity/RIV relation for nested families, while the paper only establishes that alignment in the studied nested, ordered-by-missing-information designs. It should say "in the nested families studied" or "when the more complex candidate has larger missing information."

OBJ-04.sustained_point: TV-03 is left as written. The rebuttal does not narrow the universal "every deviance and every information criterion computed from multiply imputed data" to the established object: averaged/Q-based likelihood deviance or IC, in expectation, under the estimated-scale congenial-MI conditions. "For such a model" scopes the model class but not the criterion class or expectation-level nature of the bias.
